rule.description: A shared registry record with two or more function-pointer capability members forces every registered output-format module to accept and implement capabilities it never exercises. A slot counts as a violation when its filler is a non-implementation: a null-capability stub (discards arguments, returns a null/zero constant), a forwarding filler (forwards all parameters in order to another function), a pass-through filler (returns one of its own arguments), or an absent slot (no initializer or explicit null). Slot counting includes nested record members; arrays of provider records are scanned element-wise. Functions that do real work are genuine implementations.

checks.description: A capability slot of the shared format-provider record is filled by a function that implements nothing: it discards its arguments and returns null, only forwards its arguments to another function, or returns one of its own arguments; an unfilled slot (missing initializer or explicit null) is the same violation in weaker form. Detection is a Clang-Tidy AST check (module webdis, check webdis-fat-provider) applied to every translation unit that defines or consumes format providers.
checks.detected_relation: output-format module -> capability slot of the shared format-provider interface it registers through, where the slot is never exercised by that format's real dispatch paths and is filled by a non-implementation
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The interface exceeds every consumer's dependency boundary: the record forces modules to own capabilities they do not need, and the report names the exact slot, the placeholder shape and the registering module.

matches.evidence: provider 'format_provider_raw' fills capability slot 'wrap_body' with a pass-through filler: the body returns its own argument (the serialized RESP body) unchanged and only discards the wrapper parameter. raw output never wraps bodies, so the slot exists only to satisfy the shared record.

provider 'format_provider_msgpack' fills capability slot 'ws_extract' with a null-capability stub: the body discards the client and payload arguments and returns NULL. MessagePack has no WebSocket entry point, so the capability can never be exercised.

provider 'format_provider_msgpack' fills capability slot 'ws_error' with a forwarding filler: the body forwards all four arguments in order to format_default_ws_error in common.c. MessagePack has no error encoding of its own; the slot exists only to satisfy the shared record.

provider 'format_provider_msgpack' fills capability slot 'wrap_body' with a pass-through filler: the body returns its argument (the serialized MessagePack payload) unchanged and only discards the wrapper parameter.

provider 'format_provider_custom' fills capability slot 'ws_extract' with a null-capability stub: the body discards the client and payload arguments and returns NULL. Custom types (.bin/.txt/...) are served over HTTP only, so the capability can never be exercised.

provider 'format_provider_custom' fills capability slot 'ws_error' with a forwarding filler: the body forwards all four arguments in order to format_default_ws_error in common.c. Custom types are HTTP-only; the slot exists only to satisfy the shared record.

provider 'format_provider_custom' fills capability slot 'wrap_body' with a pass-through filler: the body returns its argument (the raw payload handed to the reply sender) unchanged and only discards the wrapper parameter.
